text:
54% of US adults use AI assistants regularly. But only 24% would let one make a purchase for them.

People are happy to use bots for tasks but hold back when money is involved.

veda.ng/agentcommerce

Papers mentioning "large language model" went from 3,248 in 2018 to 96,984 in 2025. That's 29.9x.

Most of that happened after 2022. 12.2x in just three years. Good luck keeping up.

veda.ng/stateofai

Deal volume dropped by half since 2021. You'd expect smaller rounds and valuations. The opposite happened.

Median check sizes hit all-time highs at Pre-Seed, Seed, Series A, and Series B. Details at veda.ng/funding on why less money is flowing but bets are getting bigger.

Companies building picks and shovels for AI agents raised over $5B combined. See the 8-layer stack breakdown at veda.ng/agentstack where well-funded players compete.

Cerebras IPO'd at $52B. Together AI hit $1B ARR. Fireworks does 15T tokens/day. Modal grew 5x in 8 months.

Blockchain research papers went from 176 in 2013 to 20,668 in 2025. That is 118x growth in twelve years.

Read the full analysis at veda.ng/stateofweb3 showing that 82.7% of all papers were published from 2020 onward, with researchers focused on deployment-ready work.

Payment security (32%) and privacy (26%) are the top concerns about letting AI buy for you. The latest study at veda.ng/agentcommerce shows 30% of people need complete data control before they would consider letting an agent make purchases.

About 944,000 papers published in 2025 mentioned AI methods. That is 42.6% more than 2024.

However, analysis of the dataset at veda.ng/stateofai shows 48.9% of these papers got zero citations, meaning nearly half of all AI research goes unread.

In 2015 the median Seed check was $440K across 8,821 rounds. By 2026 it hit $2.8M across 4,199 rounds.

You can read about these larger rounds and bigger checks at veda.ng/funding where investors are writing fewer checks but making each one count more.

Three out of four standalone agent security companies got acquired in 18 months, including Lakera for $300M.

Check out the breakdown at veda.ng/agentstack to see how security is being built directly into code and identity workflows.

DeFi paper mentions grew from 7 in 2019 to 516 in 2025, while NFT mentions peaked in 2023.

The report at veda.ng/stateofweb3 shows that academic interest follows real utility rather than market hype.

Projections for the agentic commerce market size by 2030 range from $218B to $5T.

This 23x gap shows that nobody really knows how big it will get. Read the analysis of these projections at veda.ng/agentcommerce

China and the US started at near-parity in AI research in 2013, but by 2025 China published 53% more papers than the US.

However, analysis at veda.ng/stateofai shows the US still leads in large language model papers with 47,363 publications vs 35,923 from China.

In 2015, 17.7% of Seed-funded startups raised a Series A, but by 2023 that conversion rate dropped to 7.8%.

Read about the venture market changes at veda.ng/funding where Series A investors now expect milestones that used to be Series B territory.

Coding agents alone represent over $28B in valuation across Cognition, Factory, and CodeRabbit.

See where coding agents fit in the market at veda.ng/agentstack where they lead all other agent verticals.

Quantum resistant and post-quantum keywords grew quickly in blockchain research over the last three years.

The study at veda.ng/stateofweb3 shows that researchers are actively preparing for quantum computers to break traditional elliptic curve cryptography.

Six competing protocols are now live for how AI agents shop and pay.

I break down the features of MCP, A2A, ACP, x402, and MPP at veda.ng/agentcommerce as the market works toward picking a standard.

India AI research output grew 32.3x between 2013 and 2025, faster than both China and the US.

The report at veda.ng/stateofai shows that in 2025 India produced more papers than Japan and the UK combined.

The venture capital Gini coefficient reached 0.916 in 2026, meaning the top 1% of deals absorb over 90% of global capital.

Read the analysis of how the top 1% of deals absorb over 90% of global capital at veda.ng/funding

Out of 173 companies building agentic commerce products, only 7 focus on user interfaces.

Check out the full market map at veda.ng/agentcommerce to see why the focus remains heavily on infrastructure and wallets.

The ten fastest-rising AI research keywords are all related to large language models.

The report at veda.ng/stateofai shows DeepSeek leading keyword growth followed by RAG and security terms like jailbreak.

When a bot is the buyer, standard marketing spend like display ads and checkout design stops working.

Explore how brands are adapting to machine-readable specs and answer engine optimization at veda.ng/agentcommerce

Over 60% of AI research papers are published as open access compared to the 28% academic average.

I look at how arXiv and preprint culture keep AI research accessible at veda.ng/stateofai

The most cited AI paper is ResNet with over 221,000 citations.

Analysis at veda.ng/stateofai shows that reusable building blocks like Adam and AlexNet get cited far more than specific applications.
